newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast crudes edge up, with May trade over.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast crudes edge up, with May trade over.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude markets ended slightly higher Wednesday after fluctuating in a narrow range that tracked West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI) prices, traders said.
No new deals or negotitions were reported by traders, who waited on the sidelines to evaluate their supply needs for next month.
"I think (trade is) pretty much over for the major players," said a key seller of Alaska North Slope (ANS), the West Coast benchmark grade.
The key seller said he would continue to offer at $0.95 off May for May delviery.

The seller declined comment on whether his company had increased ANS shipments to the eastern U.S. via All-American pipeline, a move many buyers saw a helping prop of the company's offer price, despite weakening market conditions.
After easing five cents early, outright prices for May ANS ended 10 cents higher than yesterday in line with increases in spot May WTI.
On a notional basis, Line 63 was talked $2.37/2.27 under May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing (WTI). The grade rarely trades off WTI.

The city of Los Angeles on Wednesday agreed to drop all legal cases involving the Pacific Pipeline, which will carry 130,000 barrels-per-day of heated California crude oil from central California to L.A. refiners.
Traders reported no deals in Line 63 and heavy California grades.
